history_vintages.why: 'JPMorgan Chase & Co. ... is a leading global financial services firm and one of the largest banking institutions in the United States' 'JPMorgan Chase’s results of operations could be adversely affected by U.S. and international markets and economic conditions.' 'The Firm’s consumer businesses are particularly affected by domestic economic conditions' 'There is increasing competition in the financial services industry which may adversely affect JPMorgan Chase’s results of operations.' (FY2006 10-K); DURABLE, risk 2: the 10-K ties results to markets and the economy, a cycle and a competitive field, and does not call its own business cyclical (its one use of the word is for consumer loan losses: the LOW and SHW reading); no theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a bank holding company on these dates (OFFSHORE is scoped to IT services), so the watch list is empty and these words stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

eps_first_excluded.2002: a distorted year (the AAPL FY2002 test): the special items the FY2002 10-K lists ($1,210M of merger and restructuring costs, the $1,300M Enron-related surety and litigation charge and $98M of excess real estate, $1,721M after tax) exceed the year's $1,514M income from continuing operations as the FY2006 10-K restates it ($0.73 a diluted share); the operating EPS without them ($1.66) was published before that restatement, on the earlier basis (the UNP trucking rule), so the history and the P/E window start with FY2003
